title: Two supervisors voted City money to the employer that had paid them months before

beats.text: January 2025. Danny Sauter takes his seat on the Board of Supervisors.
27 days later, he votes on a contract with the nonprofit that had just paid his salary.
This is a lead, not a finding.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: Two supervisors voted City money to employers that had paid them months before. How much in all?

visual.label: Two supervisors, two recent employers
visual.sub: both voted aye; neither recusal is on record

beats.text: 80,911,804 dollars, in contract ceilings, not money paid.

visual.kicker: approved by the two votes: ceilings, not money paid

beats.text: The first lead. Sauter’s first statement lists salary from Richmond District Neighborhood Center.

beats.text: The rule: 500 dollars or more of income in the prior twelve months is a financial interest.

beats.text: And the center is the named party in the file.
The second lead. Alan Wong joined the Board in December 2025.
His statement for 2025 lists over 100,000 dollars in salary from Children’s Council of San Francisco.

visual.text: Children’s Council of San Francisco · salary Over $100,000 · “Senior Director of Public Policy Communication”

beats.text: Was any of that salary paid after 21 July 2025?
The statement gives the year’s total, not the dates of pay.
The third lead. The Ethics Commission’s recusal list holds one notice from a supervisor.

beats.text: Both roll calls print all eleven members as aye.
In February 2026, the Ethics Commission fined a Planning Commissioner under the same test.
How much?
12,000 dollars, for four votes.

beats.text: A new supervisor may not have connected a former employer’s contract on a long agenda.
What would settle it? The meeting minutes and video, and the date Wong’s pay ended.

cards.what: The minutes and video of 4 February 2025 and 21 July 2026
The date Wong’s employment and pay ended

beats.text: No authority has made a finding, and neither supervisor was asked.
A lead is a question, not an accusation.
